sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in Dickson County
sections.html:
Dickson County splits the work three ways. The Assessor of Property sets each parcel's value. The Trustee mails the bills and collects. The twelve-member county commission picks the rate while passing the budget.

You will find the assessor inside the Administration Building, 4 Court Square, Charlotte (P.O. Box 270, phone (615) 789-7015). The trustee keeps a counter on the same courthouse square, 4 Court Square (P.O. Box 220, phone (615) 789-7006), plus a branch within the County Government Building, 303 Henslee Drive, Dickson, at (615) 446-8293, option 3. Doors open at eight and shut at four, Monday to Friday.

Checks sent by mail belong at P.O. Box 246, Charlotte, TN 37036. A drop box sits at the Henslee Drive branch.

A Dickson County tax year begins with a January 1 snapshot of each parcel and ends with a payment window that closes in late February. Owners mostly care about the last two rows of this table, yet the earlier rows show when a value might move.

Dickson County property tax calendar
DateWhat happens
January 1Ownership and condition of each parcel are fixed for the year
By May 20Assessors finish the roll and mail notices of change
June 1Local equalization board opens for value complaints
Early OctoberBills mailed; payments accepted from the first Monday
February 28Final day before interest starts
March 1Unpaid balances turn delinquent

The January 1 owner of record is who the bill names. If you sell in July, the buyer may be sent a courtesy copy, yet the lien follows the land. The trustee takes installments on the current year if the last one lands before March. ACH prepayment is also offered.

Starting March 1, an open balance picks up one and a half percent each month. The trustee calls that 18 percent a year. If twelve months go by, the file moves to the Chancery Court and a delinquent tax attorney, whose suit costs and fees land on top of the interest. The last step in that suit is a tax sale of the parcel.

Behind on taxes and thinking of selling? Say so to the title company right away. It can pay the arrears from your proceeds at closing, long before any court filing. A cash sale with a short closing is one quick route.

Bankruptcy follows another track. When the notice arrives, a deputy in the trustee's office files a claim. Federal law then blocks collection of real or personal property tax until the case is dismissed or discharged, and payment typically comes through an installment plan the bankruptcy court has approved.

Before closing day, the title company will ask the trustee for a payoff figure. That figure shifts at the first of each month while interest is running, so get it dated close to the closing. If a payment is made in the final week, ask the trustee's counter for a written receipt and pass a copy to the title officer. That avoids a surprise line on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: Who pays when the house is sold?
sections.html:
Tax left unpaid at closing becomes the buyer's responsibility. The purchase contract and settlement statement spell out how the current bill is divided. Ask the title company for the proration line before signing and read it against your own bill.

No bill in the mailbox? Phone the trustee at (615) 789-7006 and request a duplicate. Not receiving a bill never erases the debt. Escrow does not change that: hand the bill to your lender, since the county never mails it there.

After closing, your buyer's deed is recorded with the Register of Deeds at 4 Court Square (P.O. Box 130, phone (615) 789-5123). Electronic recording is available through Simplifile, CSC and ePN. If the bill shows a misspelled name or wrong mailing address, the assessor makes that correction.

Start with the Local Board of Equalization. The trustee's FAQ says hearings take place in the opening two weeks of June. Appointments are made through the assessor. The state calendar lists June 1 as opening day, so phone early. A chat with the assessor may settle things faster, though it does not replace a formal appeal. Lose at the local level and you can petition the State Board of Equalization. Filing closes August 1 or 45 days after the local notice, whichever is later.

  • Houses and farmland are assessed at 25 percent of appraised value, business property at 40 percent
  • Tax equals assessed value divided by 100, then multiplied by the rate

Bring the notice of change, comparable sales and photos of any defects. If the house needs repairs that a buyer will price in, photos of those repairs make the case for a lower value.

sections.h2: Steps to take before you list
sections.html:
Four quick tasks keep a Dickson County sale moving. Ring the trustee for today's balance, prior years included. Ask the assessor to check the name and mailing address attached to your parcel. If you dispute the value, see whether the June hearing window is still open. Then tell the title company if a lender escrows your tax, because that changes who writes the check at closing.

Pull together your most recent bill, any notice of change and the deed you took title under. Those papers settle most questions a buyer or title officer will ask. A cash purchase uses the same papers and often closes sooner, since no lender has to approve the file.

sections.h2: State tax relief for seniors and disabled owners
sections.html:
The state pays back part of the tax for some seniors, disabled owners and disabled military service members. For 2026 the income limit is $38,470 (2025 income of everyone on the deed), and relief reaches up to $33,600 of market value. Owners with a qualifying service-connected rating skip the income test and have a $175,000 cap.

The trustee has the application. Request it when the 2026 bill comes out and file promptly, because the window closes five weeks after the delinquency date.

sections.h2: Dickson County housing at a glance
sections.html:
About 58,662 people live in Dickson County, 8.0 percent above the 2020 count, in 25,011 housing units. Owners occupy roughly 80.3 percent of homes. The median home value is $306,400 and the median rent is $1,015. Builders pulled 590 permits in 2025, so new construction competes with resale listings.

A house with tax owing, an inherited house and a house in need of work all call for the same prep: balance from the trustee, valuation from the assessor, both in hand before you name a price.

faqs.q: When can I start paying Dickson County property tax?
faqs.a: Payments open the first Monday of October. You can pay interest-free until February ends. From March 1 the account is delinquent.

faqs.q: Where can I pay my Dickson County tax bill in person?
faqs.a: Go to the trustee's counter on the Charlotte courthouse square or the branch at 303 Henslee Drive in Dickson, eight to four on weekdays. By mail, use P.O. Box 246, Charlotte, TN 37036. Local banks take full current-year payments.

faqs.q: Do I owe tax if I buy a Dickson County house mid-year?
faqs.a: Possibly, since the purchaser carries any tax unpaid at closing. Your settlement statement shows who covers which part of the year.

faqs.q: When does the Dickson County board of equalization meet?
faqs.a: Early June, for about two weeks. Book through the assessor at (615) 789-7015. The state calendar gives June 1 as the start date.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for state property tax relief in Dickson County?
faqs.a: Owners 65 and older, and disabled owners, with 2025 income up to $38,470. Disabled military service members and some surviving spouses face no income cap. File with the Dickson County Trustee.
